newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The trading of options and other derivatives were the worst affected area of the stock market yesterday as investors tried to understand the different role of these products after the new tax regime announced in the Federal Budget. Analysts believe the wide impact of the regime will include an impact on liquidity in the Australian market, corporate strategies, and fund managers' investment strategies. Page 1.

Newcrest Mining Ltd announced yesterday that John Quinn, who has been with the company for 27 years, had resigned as managing director after "differences" with the board. Quinn's resignation comes at the end of a disastrous 18 month period for the company, whch has seen its share price fall by more than half. Page 1.

In the lead up to next week's float on the Australian Stock Exchange, Colonial Ltd is expected to offer institutions about 150 million shares priced between A$3.00 and A$3.10 a share. Funds managers said yesterday that institutional investors will need to bid at those prices to get shares as a result of huge demand. Page 19.

IPAC Securities, one of Australia's leading financial planning firms, has sold a 50 percent interest to the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, in a move reflecting the growing trend of the institutionalisation of financial planning in Australia. While no pice was disclosed, the deal was said to have been triggered by strategic issues. Page 19.

Engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd has the support of overseas investors to bid to join a potential joint venture consisting of a large part of the company's disastrous stable of European-based Holter operations. Chief executive Peter Sancliffe said yesterday a number of parties were expected to make firm offers. Page 20.

Campbell Anderson, managing director of mining and forestry group North Ltd, told an investor briefing in London yesterday that the company is targeting a large lift in shareholder returns over the long-term, and said North was hoping to achieve earnings at a sustainable rate of between 15 and 20 percent on shareholder funds. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's A$60 billion market for share-based derivatives has been thrown into turmoil following the Federal Budget's taxation changes. The changes affect the risk management products and market activity was low yesterday as market players tried to unerstand the impact of the changes. Page 19.

As analysts said yesterday the Federal Budget did little to promote Australia's image as a regional investment centre, this disappointment led to increasingly weak financial markets. Moody's Investment Services and Standard and Poor's both rated the Budget as giving Australia no chance of upgrading its credit rating. Page 19.

The Federal Budget crackdown on dividend streaming may affect Westpac Banking Corp's proposed A$500 million preference share issue for its A$1.4 billion bid for the Bank of Melbourne. As a tax official confirmed possible problems for Westpac yesterday, the bank announced a first half profit of A$638 million, up 12.9 percent. Page 19.

Minera Escondida, the operator of the Escondida copper mine in Chile, which is 57.5 percent owned by BHP and 30 percent owned by RTZ-CRA, may go ahead with a A$130 million plan for the two-stage expansion of copper concentrate production to 175,000 tonnes per day following approval from the Chilean Regional Commission of the Environment. Page 20.

Healthscope Ltd deputy chairman Richard England announced yesterday the hospitals group's first stage of a bid to sell the Mildura Private Hospital for A$10.7 million to the Mildura District Hospital Fund. England said the proceeds would go towards reducing a debt of over A$44 million. Page 20.

Contract wine maker Simeon Wines Ltd will invest A$20 million over six years to increase production capacity at the Buronga Hill winery to 100,000 tonnes. While announcing a 1996/97 net profit of A$3.5 million, managing director Neil MacKenzie said the company had mainly completed its 1997 vintage and would crush a record 57,000 tonnes of grapes at Buronga Hill. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Westpac Banking Corp's acquisition of the Trust Bank of New Zealand was behind the company's 13 percent jump in its March-half profit to A$638 million. The figures, announced yesterday, masked a far less impressive underlying earnings performance as interest margins tumbled and amid negligible growth in lending and deposits. Page 29.

Former RTZ-CRA problem fixer Ian Johnson will replace Newcrest Mining managing director John Quinn in an effort to boost market confidence in the gold producer. The market responded well to the move, with shares jumping 25 cents to close at A$3.46. Page 9.

During a private briefing with South Australian Senator Chris Schacht and South Australian Opposition Leader Mike Rann, top Mitsubishi executives joined other Australian car manufacturers in warning the Federal Government that Australia could lose its entre car industry if the recommendations by the Productivity Commission to cut car tariffs by five percent by 2004 are adopted. Page 29.

Economists disagree with Prime Minister John Howard, and do not believe the budget has created a climate that will see the Reserve Bank lowering interest rates. They say the government's robust forecasts of a four percent rise in wages shows the Reserve Bank would not consider rate decreases; instead they expect interest rates to rise over the next six months. Page 29.

The weak property market in Canberra and the poor quality of property for sale may restrict the Federal Government's plans to sell A$800 million of Commonwealth property. The government announced in the budget its intention to sell 57 properties over the next two years. Page 33.

Following Federal Government reforms of superannuation, in-house funds are expected to be dropped by at least 10 percent of Australia's top 100 companies amid increased competition in the industry. Analysts believe the decision to force employers to offer their staff a minimum choice of five super funds will lead to each fund suffering a rise in marketing and administration costs. Page 33.
THE AGE

Operations in New Zealand and one-off gains from property sales boosted Westpac Banking Corp's interim net profit to a surprisingly high A$618 million yesterday. The result is a 13.4 percent improvement on last year. Page B1.

Newcrest Mining Ltd managing director John Quinn has been an obvious victim of the company's recent failings in the sharemarket after it was announced yesterday that Quinn's resignation was accepted at a board meeting. Investors welcomed his departure, with shares rising 25 cents to A$3.46. Page B1.

Shares in Macquarie Bank slipped as much as 26 cents yesterday to A$9.28, recovering to finish at A$9.44 in response to the Federal Government's crackdown on the trading of dividend tax credits. Brokers said yesterday that the crackdown would close down financial deals worth million of dollars in turnover. Page B1.

For the second time in six weeks, the Commonwealth Bank has bought into a specialist organisation, this time with a 50 percent share of niche financial planner and portfolio manager IPAC Securities. The undisclosed deal is the bank's first foray into reail financial planning. Page B3.

Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron said yesterday that people cannot continue to assume that unusual share trading pointed to insider trading. Speaking to the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Cameron said the sharemarket was not "infected" by widespread insider trading. Page B3.

News Corporation shares fell to their lowest level this year yesterday amid market fears the company would issue new preference shares to raise up to A$2 billion to buy The Family Channel and the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team. The slump coincided with the launch in the United States of a A$6.4 billion lawsuit by New Corp's prospective satellite partner, EchoStar. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
